hook: Michael J. Jones earned his PhD from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1997. Working with Paul Viola, he co-developed the Viola-Jones object detection framework, published as Rapid Object Detection using a Boosted Cascade of Simple Features in 2001, which combined Haar-like features, an integral image representation and a cascade of boosted classifiers to make real-time face detection possible on ordinary hardware for the first time. The pair extended the work into Robust Real-Time Face Detection in 2004. Jones continued his career at Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories, where he became a Distinguished Research Scientist working on computer vision, machine learning and data analytics, including detection and analysis of people in images and video.

Co-invented the Viola-Jones object detection framework with Paul Viola in 2001
Distinguished Research Scientist at Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories
